name: Question 2
problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve   $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,,\,2{cos}^{2}⁡t⟩$  at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{6}.$
worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{6}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({cos}^{2}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-4\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6}) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{6},\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{6},\,-4\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{6}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{6}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\,-\frac{1}{2},\,-4\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\,-\frac{1}{2},\,-\sqrt{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6}):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6})‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})}^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}+(-\sqrt{3})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{4}+3} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6})$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at the point where $\frac{\pi }{6}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\frac{\pi }{6}) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6})}{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6})‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\text{ }⟨\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\,-\frac{1}{2},\,-\sqrt{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4},\,-\frac{1}{4},\,-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
